one_line_summary: A minimal Chrome/Firefox extension that lets each tab have its own idle sleep schedule, so you can put a noisy tab to bed without touching the OS sleep settings.
problem: When you keep a dozen tabs open, the noisy ones keep waking the machine, draining battery, or eating attention, and the OS-level sleep settings don't let you pick per-tab behavior.
audience: Non-developer: people who want quieter, more battery-friendly browsing without learning about site settings or installing heavy tab managers.
solution: A lightweight extension that adds a small 'sleep' control per tab, remembers a per-tab idle timer, and suspends activity for that tab by hiding it or flagging it as dismissed until you wake it. Configuration is a simple per-site default plus per-tab overrides.
key_features: Per-tab sleep toggle and idle timer
Sleep/wake state shown in the tab and in a small popup
Option to auto-sleep tabs that have been idle longer than N minutes
No remote calls; everything stored locally in extension storage
mvp_scope: popup with per-tab sleep control, per-site defaults, idle-based auto-sleep for configurable minutes, storage of state, wake-up restores visibility/activity indicator.
tests_plan: Unit test the idle-time bookkeeping and policy lookup in a small Node test harness that mimics the background script helpers
Test per-site default resolution order (per-tab overrides site default)
Test that sleep/wake round-trip preserves the tab's policy and idle time

files.manifest.json: MV3 manifest with permissions for storage and tab capture model (no host permissions needed beyond what the extension UI needs)
files.background.js: Idle timer bookkeeping, per-tab and per-site policy resolution, sleep/wake actions
files.popup.html + popup.js + popup.css: Popup UI for sleep/wake and per-site defaults
files.content.js: Optional content-side indicator that a tab is sleeping and wake-up notification
files.lib/policy.js: Pure logic: resolve effective policy for a tab id + site
files.lib/idle.js: Pure logic: idle time bookkeeping, auto-sleep decisions
files.tests/run_tests.sh: Runs node tests (no browser required for MVP logic tests)
files.README.md: What it does, install, usage, limitations
files.RESULTS.md: Actual observed MVP results and test output
